claims.statement: Both pinned upstream RTIC C6 examples compile unmodified with Rust1.96.0 and the unchanged tracked lockfile.
claims.scope: RTIC f1797184, HAL=1.0.0-rc.0, release target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf; monotonic and sw_and_hw only.

Original packaging failures and separately corrected image metadata remain retained. sw_and_hw has no physical result.

claims.statement: The first scheduled RTIC monotonic attempt fails frozen v1 after a second ROM startup; two later attempts were not run.
claims.scope: One warm-reset attempt of the exact unmodified example plus selected corrected-header bootloader/app images; no method change or replacement.
limitations: All seven expected markers precede the restart, but successful subsets do not qualify the failed attempt.
No second reset-reason line was retained, so cause remains unconfirmed. This does not establish universal C6/RTIC incompatibility.

claims.statement: Seven expected RTIC application markers and coarse timer-dependent resumption are observed before the additional startup that fails qualification.
claims.scope: UART0 output and host-receipt pacing for three cooperative priority-zero futures, diagnostic subsets of the failed v1 attempt only.
limitations: This remains a failed qualification, with no completed twelve-second guard or continued-liveness claim.
No device clock readback/calibration, GPIO interrupt response, positive-priority preemption, CPU/energy efficiency or global memory-peak result.

claims.statement: Two frozen IDF finite-load qualification boots retain all 4,032 nominal releases, checked completions, generator misses, queue-full losses and synthetic deadline outcomes.
claims.scope: One radio-off board, one disabled and one enabled runtime-statistics profile, two generator controls and four 250 ms work pulses per boot; before/after task and allocator indicators accompany the pulses.
limitations: Qualification profiles have no paired estimator or profile-effect comparison. Finite pulse outcomes do not establish sustainable capacity, fairness, starvation freedom, product deadlines or a platform ranking.
Software timer generation is measured and bounded for these pulses, without external frequency calibration. Generator misses remain explicit rather than being hidden or replaced.
Enabled counters include ISR spans and boundary intervals; snapshots are outside the offer/drain window. These are not exclusive CPU utilization or global simultaneous heap/stack peaks.
The harness reserves 48,384 bytes of job records and 8,928 bytes of snapshots in both Rust layouts. Application headroom and hardware integration remain unqualified.

claims.statement: Three frozen IDF diagnostic boots distinguish a blocked worker from checked busy work and retain before/held/freed indicators for a touched 16 KiB allocation.
claims.scope: The selected U64 esp_timer task-attribution path and MALLOC_CAP_8BIT allocator observations only; six fixed snapshots per boot with gross collection endpoints and stack-fill indicators.
limitations: Task counters include ISR spans and unflushed current-task intervals. Signed boundary residuals are not idle time; this is not physical CPU busy/idle or exclusive ISR accounting.

Allocator/stack-fill observations do not establish global simultaneous peaks, pressure/fragmentation behavior, application headroom or a qualified stack-depth bound. Output/join allocation costs follow these snapshots.
No instrumentation-on/off comparison, sustainable arrival-rate capacity, external frequency calibration, energy measurement or platform ranking is supplied.

claims.statement: The bare-metal calibration image completed checked compute/observer captures.
claims.scope: Initial and clocked bare-metal compute controls on the attached C6, not full CPU/IRQ qualification.
limitations: Initial runtime flash frequency was unverified; integer computation does not establish CPU utilization, interrupt behavior or an OS ranking.

claims.statement: Clocked bare-metal captures contain before/after CPU and flash register snapshots.

claims.statement: The alignment probe observes 308 versus 282–283 microsecond medians with matching workload instruction bytes.

limitations: This does not isolate a cache-miss mechanism, exact fetch penalty, usable memory or persistent-storage correctness.
